ai_view.directive: Follow as written. Every fairness assumption must earn independent qualification before it may restrict the executions the model checker examines. All four gates required; three of four is failure.
ai_view.specification: Build the Fairness Assumption Audit Protocol (FAAP) as a stacked spec on naya5/fairness-verification: assumption registry with immutable versioned identity, four gates (independent justification, satisfiability, minimal sufficiency, non-circularity), assumption-change sensitivity reports, machine-readable audit receipts, adversarial scheduler substitution test, conditional versioned qualification. No new Brain or authority layer: CONNECT traces dependencies, PROVE binds evidence and witnesses, VERIFY runs the checks, LAW governs sufficiency for use.

intelligence.applicability: Every fairness qualification in NayaNET, every scheduler version, every assumption set. Applies to the fairness-verification stack and its future wiring into live PROVE/CONNECT/VERIFY.
connections: SN-0771 fairness verification (parent layer: assumption hygiene, vacuity detection, AssumptionContract)
decisions: Shawn's explicit framework, main chat, 2026-10-10. His word IS the verification (Verification Law).
Dispatched to build immediately as naya5/fairness-assumption-audit stacked on naya5/fairness-verification.
No new Brain or independent authority layer per his framework: CONNECT/PROVE/VERIFY + LAW governance only.
intelligence.essence: Every fairness assumption must have an independent reason to be believed, a satisfiable and meaningful scope, a demonstrated role in the proof, and a justification that does not depend on the conclusion it is supposed to support. An assumption must not eliminate a scheduler failure unless NayaNET can independently establish that the excluded behavior is genuinely outside the environment being qualified. The highest-value safeguard is the adversarial scheduler test: if NayaNET can make an intentionally unfair scheduler look fair merely by strengthening its assumptions, the assumption audit must reject that qualification.
intelligence.falsifier: A fairness qualification that passes while an assumption quietly removes the exact starvation scenario the scheduler was supposed to handle; a circular assumption (scheduler self-report as its own fairness justification) accepted as independent; UNKNOWN converted into PASS by an aggregate score.

human_view.meaning: Before we trust a fairness proof, we interrogate every assumption it rests on. Each assumption must prove four things: it has an independent reason to be believed, it allows at least one real execution, it is actually needed for the proof, and it doesn't secretly assume the very fairness we're trying to prove. Miss any one of the four and the qualification fails. The killer test: swap in a deliberately unfair scheduler — if the assumptions still make it look fair, the assumptions are doing the cheating, not the scheduler doing the work.

intelligence.learning_lesson: Assumption hygiene (SN-0772) sketched the boundary; FAAP makes it a machine. The recurring failure mode across the stack is the same: the model gets constrained until the proof passes, and nobody records what was excluded. FAAP's sensitivity report (what each assumption excludes) is the permanent antidote.

machine_view.spec_only: Framework ratified; spec branch naya5/fairness-assumption-audit to be built and tested. Not wired into live paths until the integration phases reach it.

intelligence.measurement_contract: Ten acceptance tests, each with positive controls: (1) independently established resource guarantee -> eligible for conditional use; (2) scheduler self-report as justification -> REJECT; (3) contradictory assumptions -> UNSATISFIABLE; (4) no recurring eligibility admitted -> VACUOUS_FOR_TARGET; (5) redundant assumption removed, proof holds -> REDUNDANT; (6) removal exposes genuine starvation -> record NECESSARY relative to model; (7) hidden semantic dependency -> CIRCULAR; (8) unfair scheduler passes due to assumptions -> flag masking risk, reject unqualified PASS; (9) checker timeout in minimization -> MINIMALITY_UNKNOWN; (10) passes under justified non-vacuous audited set -> QUALIFIED_IN_MODEL_SCOPE. UNKNOWN stays UNKNOWN.

naya_view.directive: Register every fairness assumption as a reviewable object with immutable versioned identity: predicate, scope, owner, control_boundary, justification_refs, dependency_refs, counterexamples_excluded, satisfiability_witness, necessity_result, circularity_result, verifier_receipt. Run all four gates. Record what each assumption excludes. Version the qualification with scheduler version, obligation class, environment, and assumption set. Never report a bare PASS.

simple_view.meaning: Don't let the proof cheat by quietly ruling out the hard cases. Every assumption gets interrogated: why should I believe you, do you allow real examples, are you actually needed, and are you secretly assuming what we're trying to prove?

intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor inherits the four-gate discipline and the registry contract, so it cannot be talked into a vacuous fairness proof by a plausible-sounding assumption set.
intelligence.uncertainty: The framework is ratified; the spec is not yet built. Open design questions from his text: how audit evidence is versioned, how audit boundaries are enforced at runtime, and the exact machine procedure for checking assumptions — the build coordinator answers these.
